benchmark_hit_summary.basis: F-0011 and F-0021 both land on the masked message path in competition kmac.sv. Direct source inspection confirms that the EnMasking branch no longer uses the entropy-derived msg_mask value and instead hardwires a constant all-ones mask.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: In the competition RTL EnMasking branch, `static_mask` is hardwired to all ones at kmac.sv:911, `msg_mask_permuted` is derived from `static_mask` rather than from the entropy output at kmac.sv:915-920, and the final masked data path XORs each share with `static_mask` at kmac.sv:923-926. The fresh entropy-derived `msg_mask` is therefore removed from the active masked message path.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: Masking enabled (`EnMasking == 1`) with message masking active (`cfg_msg_mask == 1`).
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: The masked message path becomes deterministic instead of freshness-dependent, weakening the intended side-channel masking hardening for repeated physical observations.
evidence: kmac.sv:919 computes `msg_mask_permuted[i] = static_mask[RndCnstMsgPerm[i]]`, so the permutation no longer depends on entropy.
kmac.sv:925-926 applies `({MsgWidth{cfg_msg_mask}} & static_mask)` to every share, bypassing the entropy-generated `msg_mask` path entirely.
